old: 'pippalī' is not glossed beyond the name here (it is the thing drawn out of the dried fruits; the identity is not stated). 'palala' literally paste (also flesh/sesame paste in dictionaries); kept as a name. The pot is understood to be filled with the rubbed pippalīs. Identification: bare 'pippalī' is long pepper (Piper longum; standard). Here, in the chapter on madana, the 'pippalīs' drawn out of the dried fruits and called 'phalapippalī' in the next units are probably the dried madana fruit pieces themselves (the commentators' reading, as far as I recall; probable, not certain), so 'long pepper' is not put in the translation. 'palala' is ground sesame paste in some references (kept as the name palala).
new: 'pippalī' is not glossed beyond the name here (it is the thing drawn out of the dried fruits; the identity is not stated). Here, in the chapter on madana, the 'pippalīs' drawn out of the dried fruits and called 'phalapippalī' in the next units are probably the dried madana fruit pieces themselves (read from the context: the pieces are drawn out of the dried madana fruits, are later called phalapippalī, and are kept apart from the kernel, majjā; not checked against a commentary; probable, not certain), so 'long pepper' is not put in the translation. why: reviewer (error): Unverifiable attribution from memory written into a project note (no commentary was consulted). The phalapippalī = dried madana fruit pieces reading itself is sound and tagged probable (see summary).

old: Or the decoction of the fruit kernel, with an addition of vatsaka (kuṭaja) and the rest, mixed with the decoction of either nimba (neem) or arka (swallow-wort), removing all Kapha ailments arising from satiation (saṃtarpaṇa).
new: Or the decoction of the fruit kernel, with an addition of vatsaka (kuṭaja) and the rest, mixed with the decoction of either nimba (neem) or arka (Calotropis, madar), removing all Kapha ailments arising from satiation (saṃtarpaṇa).
why: reviewer (minor): 'Swallow-wort' is ambiguous in English (also Chelidonium, Cynanchum); the plant is Calotropis (Hindi आक), usual English madar/giant milkweed.

old: अथवा उसके कषाय से मिली हुई सुरा यानी अनाज की मदिरा को कफ, अरोचक यानी अरुचि, कास यानी खाँसी, पाण्डुरोग यानी रक्ताल्पता और यक्ष्मन् यानी क्षय रोग में प्रयोग करे।
new: अथवा उसके कषाय से मिली हुई सुरा यानी अनाज की मदिरा को कफ, अरोचक यानी अरुचि, कास यानी खाँसी, पाण्डुरोग यानी रक्ताल्पता और यक्ष्मन् यानी आज के तपेदिक सहित क्षय में प्रयोग करे।
why: reviewer (minor): In modern Hindi 'क्षय रोग' is simply tuberculosis, so the Hindi is flatter than the English ('consumption; includes what is now called tuberculosis') and silently reintroduces the यक्ष्मा problem the glossary forbids. Supportable form: wasting disease that includes today's tuberculosis.
